clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient presented with severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain and jaundice, consistent with obstructive jaundice, supported by elevated bilirubin and liver enzymes. Initial abdominal ultrasound showed cholelithiasis but a normal common bile duct, ruling out choledocholithiasis as the cause of obstruction. Subsequent ERCP revealed a mass lesion in the second part of the duodenum, preventing scope advancement, and a stent was placed to relieve obstruction. Fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the mass showed a submucosal lesion composed of epithelioid, spindle, and ganglion-like cells, with spindle cells positive for S100, synaptophysin, and chromogranin, which are characteristic findings for gangliocytic paraganglioma. During hospitalization, the patient developed suspected cholangitis, which was successfully treated with antibiotics. No further information on definitive surgical management or long-term follow-up was provided.
